body:
Coaching evidence: Kim (2018), a 40-speaker Seoul Korean spontaneous-speech study, explicitly distinguishes speaking rate (includes silent intervals) from articulation rate (removes pauses) and measures syllables/sec or sec/syllable; it also finds substantial individual variation. This directly supports applicant p9's separate syllable rate, articulation speed, and silence ratio, and argues against a universal 'too fast' threshold—calibrate per speaker/session baseline and use sustained deviations. Primary article: https://www.eksss.org/archive/view_article?pid=pss-10-4-19 ; DOI https://doi.org/10.13064/ksss.2018.10.4.019 .
Post-report architecture: append immutable session events (`slide.changed`, `transcript.final`, `speech.segment`, `card.*`, `approval.*`, `coach.alert`) with event_id/session_id/sequence/observed_at/produced_at/schema_version, then recompute projections after session. At-least-once brokers imply dedupe/idempotency. AWS transactional-outbox guidance flags duplicate messages, ordering, rollback, and recommends idempotent consumers: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/cloud-design-patterns/transactional-outbox.html . For MVP, Postgres event table + transactional outbox + Redis Streams is sufficient; do not introduce a dedicated event-store product.
summary: Coaching metric evidence and event-log report design
